sections.title: Working with AI coding tools

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: Tools such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code and Cursor are now common at work. The skill being tested isn't typing prompts; it's staying the engineer responsible for the result.

sections.title: Where they help and where to be careful

rows: Concurrency and transactions: errors look plausible
Library APIs: may be invented or outdated
Stack traces and first debugging hypotheses
Secrets and customer data: never paste them

blocks.title: Task flow
blocks.code:
flowchart LR
  A[Describe the task and constraints] --> B[Ask for a plan first]
  B --> C[Generate a small change]
  C --> D[Read every line]
  D --> E[Run tests and add missing ones]
  E --> F{Correct?}
  F -->|no| C
  F -->|yes| G[Commit and open a normal review]
blocks.caption: You remain the author: if you can't explain it, don't commit it.

blocks.code:
Add rate limiting to POST /api/orders in this Spring Boot 3 service.
Constraints: use the existing Redis connection; limit 10 requests per minute per user;
return 429 with a Retry-After header; follow the style of RateLimitFilter in the auth package.
First list the files you would change and any risks. Do not write code yet.
blocks.title: A prompt with context and constraints

sections.title: Risks to name in an interview

rows: Check that packages exist, and scan them
Follow company policy; use approved tools only
Prompt injection through files or web pages
Treat tool output as untrusted; review actions
Practise DSA and design without the tool

blocks.title: Interviews
blocks.text: Many coding rounds ban AI tools, and some test using them. Ask beforehand, and keep practising unaided.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Give context and constraints; ask for a plan first.
- Keep changes small, read all of it, and test it.
- Never paste secrets or customer data.
- You own what you commit.

items.question: "Do you use AI tools?" How do you answer?
items.answer: Give a specific example: the task, how you checked the output, a time it was wrong, and how you caught it.

items.question: AI wrote a passing test suite for your code. Is that enough?
items.answer: No. Tests can simply assert current behaviour, including bugs. Check that they would fail for a wrong implementation, and cover edge cases.
